Sentence Review: Simple Present, Present Continuous, Be Going To
Let's remember those useful structures to talk about the present and the future.

Simple present:
We use the simple present to talk about permanent habitual facts in the present.
You can use the following structure:

Subject + verb (action performed) + complement


Examples:
We work on project management.
I develop systems.

 Don't forget to add the “s” in the affirmative when you refer indirectly to a single person or thing.

Examples:
She designs the best charts in class.
The Gantt chart shows all the tasks of the project.

The negative form in the simple present are made with the verb do not which in the third person becomes does not. The main verbs of the sentence keep their base form, we do not add the “s” when we formulate negative statements. Remember that you can use the contraction form of the auxiliary verbs don't and doesn't.

Look at the following structure in negative form:

Subject + doesn't / don't + verb in base form + complement

>
Examples:
We don't know how manage that project.
She doesn't understand the first task.

To make a question, put the auxiliary do/does before the subject. Only information questions can come before the auxiliary verb.

Follow these structures when using question in simple present:

Yes/No questions
Do/Does+ subject + main verb+ complement?

Wh questions
Wh word + do/does + subject + main verb + complement?

Examples:
Does she work with us?
What tools do you use to design Gantt charts?

Remember there are compound questions as What tools, this is a w-h word with a complement.

We use present continuous to talk about actions that are happening at the moment of speaking, or/and temporary situations.
Look at the following structure in affirmative form:

Subject + verb to be ( am/is/are) + verb in gerund (-ing) + complement

Examples:
I'm working on my tasks at the moment.
This year, we're developing an amazing software system.

To make a negative statement, we just have to add the particle not next to the verb be conjugated.
Look at the following structure in negative form:

Subject + verb to be in negative ( am not /isn't /aren't ) + verb in gerund (-ing) + complement

Examples:
We aren't working on the schedule.
He is not doing anything.

To make questions in the present continuous, we put the verb be (conjugated) before the subject. Just as in the simple present, only a wh-word can come before the verb be.
Follow these structures for questions in present continuous:

Yes/No questions
Verb to be (Am/ Is / Are) + subject + verb in gerund (-ing) + complement+?

Wh questions
Wh word (What/Where/When…) + verb to be (am/ is/ are) + subject + verb in gerund (-ing) + complement+?

Examples:
Are we working on the project now?
What colors is she using to differentiate the tasks?

We use be going towhen you want to talk about plans for the future.
Take a look to the following structure:

Subject + verb to be (am/is/ are) + going to + main verb + complement


Examples:
I'm going to design the plan in a Gantt chart next week. We are going to visit the client to collect requirements next month.

To make the negative form, we add not to the verb be conjugated.
Take a look to the following structure in negative form:

Subject + verb to be (am not /isn't / aren't ) + going to + main verb + complement


Examples:
She is not going to manage that project.
We are not going to continue with that task.

For questions, we put the verb be before the subject, just as we do in the present continuous.
Follow these structures for questions with be going to:

Yes/No questions
Verb to be (Am/ Is / Are) + subject + going to + main verb+ complement+?

Wh questions

Wh word (What/Where/When…) + verb to be ( am/ is/ are) + subject + going to + main verb + complement+?


Examples:
Are we going to continue with that task?
Why are you going to quit the project?

There are two kinds of speech in English, formal and informal speech, you choose which to use depending on the person and the situation.
There are some pivotal differences between formal and informal speech

Formal speech:
We usually use formal English in books, articles, essays, and formal letters. In formal English, longer and more structuralize expressions are used, we express our demands, wishes, opinions, and so forth indirectly and keenly.

In formal English, never use contractions of verbs, or omit syllables using the apostrophe. We have to write complete words and statements. In addition, common expressions as “get” are not common in formal English, those words that come from Latin are considered more formal than the English words.

Informal speech:
 Informal English is far more common than formal English, because it is the language you use to talk to your family, and acquaintance, informal English is more familiar.

Sentences in informal English are shorter, we can use contractions, omit syllables in some words, and we talk straight forward. The most common English words and expressions are used in informal English.

We're working on system requirements at the moment, and now we can set types of requirements apart, as well as to line up a project schedule using a Gantt chart. But, do we understand what project management is? On the next lines, I'm going to explain this concept for you to read it and understand it.
To start, the concept of project management became famous in the mid-20th century as a key element in project development. Project management is a transitory undertaking aimed to create an authentic, unique product, or result. Plus, project management is temporary because projects have a delimited beginning as well as an end. The main purpose of project management is to deliver projects on time, and on-budget.

Another important fact related to project management is that it's unique. As projects aim to achieve a goal, they foster creative processes with the purpose of adapting the project to the stakeholders' requirements. In addition, a project always includes different people from different backgrounds working together to put forward an innovative brand-new product or service.
Project management is a set of operations in which stakeholders and participants apply their knowledge and skills. Consequently, they are going to use the tools they have for the project, solving shortcomings, and applying innovative techniques to satisfy project requirements.

We have already discussed project management. Now, you may ask yourself how you can write a text about this topic. Firstly, you can start with the definition of the concept; then, you can mention its characteristics. Next, you have to write clearly and don't forget that you must check the grammar. Finally, write it in formal English.
